A.explanation: This is correct physics because pushing the cylinder further in displaces water upwards and raises the water level, so some water gains $mgh$.

B.explanation: This is correct physics because the centre of mass of the wooden cylinder moves downwards when it is pushed from partially to fully submerged.

C.explanation: This is correct physics because force $F$ acts downwards and the cylinder displacement is downwards, so $W = Fs$ is positive.

D.explanation: This is not correct because upthrust acts upwards while the cylinder moves downwards, so work is done against upthrust, not by upthrust.

hints: Notice the direction of motion of the cylinder when force $F$ pushes it from partially submerged to just fully submerged.
Compare the direction of force $F$ downwards and the direction of upthrust upwards with that downward displacement.
Think about what happens to the displaced water level when more of the wooden cylinder goes below the surface.
walkthrough: Identify the displacements: the cylinder moves downwards under force $F$, while displaced water is forced upwards and the free surface rises.
Recall work done by a constant force is $W = Fs\cos\theta$, positive when force and displacement are in the same direction and negative when opposite.
Force $F$ is downwards and displacement is downwards, so $\theta = 0$ and $F$ does positive work on the cylinder.
The cylinder centre of mass moves down, so its gravitational potential energy $mgh$ decreases, and the raised water gains gravitational potential energy.
Upthrust on the cylinder is upwards but displacement is downwards, so $\theta = 180^{\circ}$ and energy is transferred against upthrust, not by it. This is option D.
